project: Automatos AI Platform — PRD-227 Board Light-Up (Auto-as-Manager wave, chain 1/6)
description: Cut from origin/main — chain position 1/6 of the Auto-as-Manager wave (map: docs/PRDS/PRD-WAVE-AUTO-MANAGER.md, seeded on this branch with the spec docs/PRDS/PRD-227-BOARD-LIGHT-UP.md). SCOPE = three wiring diffs that make existing loops visible: (US-001) agent-side board handlers emit the same SSE events human moves already emit, and gain blocked/failed status parity; (US-002) mission lifecycle narrates into the launching chat thread via the existing PRD-205 background-message seam; (US-003) the notification bell can navigate approval_grant and watch link types plus a drift guard. BAKED DECISIONS (Gerard 2026-08-27, from PRD-227 §8 proposals): narration is ON for ALL missions — non-chat-launched runs narrate to the per-user Auto thread via the existing find_or_create_auto_chat fallback; MISSION_NARRATION_TASK_CAP default 8 (task-level lines suppressed above it; run-level lines always). ANCHORS (verified 2026-08-27 — RE-VERIFY by grep before relying): agent handler orchestrator/modules/tools/discovery/handlers_board_tasks.py:258-320 (allowed statuses ~:270, NO notify call); human path notifies at orchestrator/api/board_tasks.py:912-916, blocked handling :548-553 + :898-902; notify_board_event orchestrator/services/board_events.py:38-70 (fail-soft — a NOTIFY failure never fails the caller); coordinator seams orchestrator/services/coordinator_service.py:3129 (approve_plan) + :2272 (_record_task_result); messenger orchestrator/services/chat_messenger.py:96-202 (deliver_background_message is the fail-soft producer wrapper; today's ONLY producers are watch_notifications.py:87-100 and scheduled_task_service.py:446-465); bell frontend/components/notifications/notification-bell.tsx:42-64 linkFor; the two unlinked producers write link_type at orchestrator/modules/tools/execution/tool_grants.py:412 and orchestrator/services/watch_notifications.py:75. BINDING RULES: NO new alembic revisions (acceptance-enforced); NO new tables; NO new routes (route manifest untouched); NO new SSE event names (board_changed/chat_changed only — services/board_events.py:229-231); no os.getenv outside orchestrator/config.py (MISSION_NARRATION_TASK_CAP lives in config.py); NOTIFY/narration failures must be fail-soft (never fail the tool call or the coordinator tick); canonical terms (Mission, Task, Auto is a proper noun); PURE tests (@integration skips cleanly without local Postgres; real-Postgres is CI test.yml per-story push); NEVER 'git add -A'/'git add .'/'-u' (node_modules untracked and NOT gitignored — stage explicit paths only); never 'git stash -u'. Frontend gate: cd frontend && npm run -s test green after US-003.

userStories.title: CRITICAL (review) — mission narration commits/rolls back the coordinator's SHARED session, silently destroying mission state on a chat-write failure
userStories.description: US-002 narration is NOT fail-soft the way US-001's board NOTIFY is. _narrate_mission (coordinator_service.py:398) → deliver_background_message → post_background_message → ChatService.save_message does a REAL self.db.commit() on the coordinator's own session (consumers/chatbot/service.py:469,475); on ANY exception deliver_background_message calls db.rollback() on that same session (chat_messenger.py:199). Every narration call site fires MID-transaction, before the caller commits: approve_plan (:3270), _record_task_result (:2413,:2415), cancel_mission (:3443), the tick terminal observer (:1808), approval-expiry (:2875). The transitions before them are flush-only (orchestration_state.py:163,282,394) and the real commit is the caller's (api/missions.py:1301 after approve_plan; :419 after create; the tool executor for the tool path). FAILURE: approve_plan flushes RUNNING + queued tasks (uncommitted) → save_message's commit raises (transient DB error / dropped connection / serialization failure, plausible under load since this fires on EVERY approve/cancel/task-terminal) → deliver_background_message rolls back → the RUNNING transition + RUN_APPROVED event + queued tasks are destroyed → approve_plan returns run normally → the caller commits an empty tx → the API returns HTTP 200 state='awaiting_approval' (the tool returns success:true, state:awaiting_approval — self-contradictory) and the mission is silently stuck forever. Same class: cancel_mission (cancel reverted → mission still RUNNING, keeps dispatching + burning budget while the caller was told 'cancelled') and _record_task_result (task COMPLETED/FAILED reverted → re-dispatched next tick = duplicate execution). Invisible to test_prd227_mission_narration.py because it monkeypatches deliver_background_message wholesale and passes MagicMock() as db, so the real commit/rollback semantics are never exercised. US-001's notify_board_event (board_events.py:38-68 — pg_notify SELECT only, never commit/rollback; NOTIFY buffers until the caller's commit) is the correct reference pattern narration must match.
acceptanceCriteria: DONE — _narrate_mission (coordinator_service.py:440-453) routes the chat-message write through an INDEPENDENT short-lived SessionLocal() (closed in finally), so save_message's commit AND deliver_background_message's failure-rollback land on that session, NEVER the coordinator's shared `db`. All 6 narration sites funnel through this one function (:1830,:2435,:2437,:2897,:3292,:3465 via _narrate_run_terminal). Pure tests: test_narration_delivery_runs_on_independent_session (delivery ran on the fresh session; caller.commit/rollback never called; session closed) + test_narration_failure_leaves_coordinator_session_untouched (raising delivery → caller untouched, no propagation, session still closed) — both success and failure paths.

userStories.title: HIGH (review) — mission narration target is caller-controlled (config.origin_chat_id / config.chat_id) with workspace-only scoping → cross-user chat injection within a workspace
userStories.description: The narration delivery target run.config['origin_chat_id'] is caller-controllable. handlers_missions.py:115 falls back to config['chat_id'] (a plain key inside the caller/LLM-supplied config tool-arg, never stripped) and :116 (if _origin_str and not config.get('origin_chat_id')) PRESERVES a caller-supplied config['origin_chat_id'] — it is never overwritten and never stripped, so it survives even over the server-injected origin. The executor's strip-then-inject hardening (platform_executor.py:1126-1130) guards only the top-level _origin_chat_id, never the nested config.*. The REST route POST /api/missions (api/missions.py:405,417) bypasses the executor entirely and copies body.config verbatim into coordinator.create_mission, which stores it as run.config unmodified (coordinator_service.py:2491); MissionCreateRequest.config is an unrestricted Dict[str,Any] (missions.py:83-85) and the tool schema has no additionalProperties:false (actions_missions.py:29-40). At delivery, _narrate_mission reads run.config['origin_chat_id'] (coordinator_service.py:418,427) and post_background_message honors any chat matching Chat.workspace_id — with NO Chat.user_id check (chat_messenger.py:124-137). FAILURE: any caller with missions:create (or a prompt-injected agent) creates a mission whose config.origin_chat_id (or config.chat_id on the tool path) is another workspace member's private chat uuid, and every 'Auto · mission' lifecycle line is persisted into that other user's chat — workspace-clamped (no cross-tenant) but cross-USER, violating chat_messenger's own documented 'rather than leaking across chats' invariant. Contract US-002 mandates the origin be server-injected only. (Independent reviewer rated this CRITICAL; down-rated to HIGH here because the workspace clamp blocks cross-tenant — Gerard to arbitrate.)
acceptanceCriteria: DONE — all FOUR mission-create entry points route caller config through ONE shared strip helper services.chat_messenger.strip_caller_narration_origin (fresh dict, removes origin_chat_id+chat_id): handlers_missions.create_mission (tool — origin set from _origin_chat_id(params) server value ONLY; the config['chat_id'] fallback + the caller-origin-preserving `and not config.get(...)` guard deleted; context fetch now narrows to the server _origin), api/missions.create_mission (REST), handlers_blog.create_blog_post_from_topic (the 4th caller the security review caught — agent-id created_by), and api/missions.import_mission_plan (sibling parity). ONE helper = no per-path drift (the drift that reopened the hole in the blog path). Tests: test_tool_create_strips_caller_supplied_origin_and_chat_id, test_tool_create_uses_server_injected_origin_only, test_rest_create_strips_*, test_blog_create_strips_* (asserts created_by=='42' agent-id), test_import_plan_strips_*.

userStories.title: HIGH (review) — REST/suggestion-card chat-launched missions never narrate into the launching thread; they always fall back to the Auto thread, so US-002 AC3 is unmet for the primary human 'Launch Mission' path
userStories.description: US-002 AC3 ('a chat-launched mission produces narration messages in the launching thread') is satisfied only for the TOOL path (Auto autonomously calling platform_create_mission mid-chat — the executor server-injects _origin_chat_id from caller_context.conversation_id at platform_executor.py:1126-1130, and handlers_missions.py:124-125 sets run.config['origin_chat_id']). It is NOT satisfied for the SUGGESTION-CARD REST launch — the direct human 'Launch Mission' affordance rendered inside any chat: frontend/components/chatbot/chat.tsx:977,1364 render <MissionSuggestionCard chatId={id}> where id is the CURRENT conversation (not necessarily the Auto thread); mission-suggestion-card.tsx:44-46 posts config={source:'chat', chat_id: chatId} via useCreateMission → POST /api/missions. api/missions.py:410 does mission_config = strip_caller_narration_origin(body.config), which removes chat_id and NEVER re-injects origin_chat_id (the REST path has no server-side origin capture). _narrate_mission (coordinator_service.py:421) reads only cfg.get('origin_chat_id'), so it is always absent for REST-created missions → every 'Auto · mission' lifecycle line lands in the creator's Auto thread (find_or_create_auto_chat), never the chat the user launched from. This is NOT a P227-RVW-2 regression — the pre-RVW-2 code (mission_config = dict(body.config)) preserved config['chat_id'] but never mapped it to origin_chat_id either, so this path never narrated to the launching chat; it is an original US-002 incompleteness surfaced by the RVW-2 layer. SAFE FIX: the REST caller is AUTHENTICATED (created_by=ctx.user.id, api/missions.py:421) and chat_messenger.py:176's Layer-2 owner check (int(candidate.user_id)==owner_int_id) already forces a chat_id owned by another user to fall back to Auto — so honoring the authenticated user's OWN chat_id as origin is cross-user-safe WITHOUT reopening RVW-2. The RVW-2 blanket Layer-1 strip on the authenticated REST path is over-broad: it removes the one legitimate origin-capture AC3 needs while adding zero security margin over Layer-2.
acceptanceCriteria: On the REST create path (api/missions.py::create_mission), the mission's origin_chat_id is server-set from the authenticated request's chat_id (body.config['chat_id'] or a dedicated field) so a same-user chat-launched mission narrates INTO that chat. Keep the RVW-2 discipline (strip caller keys first, then server-set origin from the authenticated identity) — do NOT simply stop stripping — and lean on the Layer-2 owner check for safety.

Cross-user safety preserved (RVW-2 NOT reopened): a REST create whose config.chat_id is owned by ANOTHER workspace user still delivers to the creator's Auto thread, 0 messages in the other user's chat (chat_messenger.py:176 Layer-2 owner check). Ensure run.created_by resolves to the authenticated user (coordinator treats created_by as a Clerk id via User.clerk_user_id lookup at coordinator_service.py:305) so the owner comparison is correct; if ctx.user.id is not the clerk id, resolve it before persisting created_by.

Test (PURE where possible): POST /api/missions with config={source:'chat', chat_id:<creator's OWN chat>} → run.config['origin_chat_id']==that chat AND narration target is that chat, not the Auto thread. Second test: config.chat_id=<another user's chat> → narration falls back to the creator's Auto thread, 0 messages in the other user's chat (mirror test_prd227_narration_target_owner.py's cross-user assertion). Neither test reintroduces a caller-controllable cross-user origin.
import_mission_plan (api/missions.py:466) parity if it can carry a legitimate origin. No new routes, no new SSE event names, no os.getenv outside config.py, narration stays fail-soft.

userStories.title: MEDIUM (review, pre-existing) — agent update_board_task_status omits the in_progress field-reset the human update_task_status endpoint performs, leaving stale completed_at/error_message/result on a redo → a succeeded task renders as failed
userStories.description: PRE-EXISTING divergence (the in_progress field lines at handlers_board_tasks.py:321-322 are UNCHANGED base context — NOT introduced by this diff) that US-001's status-parity goal should close: US-001 explicitly aligns the agent handler with the HTTP path and its own comment at handlers_board_tasks.py:336 cites api/board_tasks.py:912, the update_task_status drag endpoint. That endpoint (api/board_tasks.py:891-895) resets completed_at=None, error_message=None, result=None on every in_progress transition; the agent handler only sets started_at (and only when unset). FAILURE: a BoardTask that reached status='done' carrying a non-null error_message from a prior failed execution is redone by an agent (platform_update_task_status status='in_progress' then later 'done'); the stale error_message survives, and board-card.tsx:62 (isFailed = task.error_message != null && task.status === 'done') renders the red 'failed' strip (board-card.tsx:176-179) with the OLD error on a task that just succeeded — the board-state-lies class 'light up the board' exists to kill. The agent handler currently matches the OTHER HTTP endpoint (update_task, api/board_tasks.py:544 — guarded, no reset), so the HTTP side is itself inconsistent; mirror update_task_status since that is the status-change semantic and the one US-001's comment cites. Gerard to arbitrate scope (pre-existing, outside the diff's change surface).
acceptanceCriteria: handlers_board_tasks.py update_board_task_status clears completed_at, error_message, and result when new_status=='in_progress', mirroring api/board_tasks.py:891-895 (the update_task_status endpoint US-001's comment cites), so a redone task carries no stale terminal fields.

Test: a task with status='done' + error_message set, moved to 'in_progress' via update_board_task_status, has completed_at/error_message/result cleared; moving it back to 'done' does not render as failed (error_message stays null).
No behavior change to the blocked/failed transitions already added; VALID_STATUSES reuse, notify, and fail-soft all unchanged.
